instruction: Sort all transaction records by date in chronological order (earliest to latest).

metadata.explanation: Task requires sorting all records by Date column (column A) in ascending order. Verified with Python: dates range from 2022-11-19 to 2023-02-04, already in ascending order in source. Evaluator extracts column A dates and verifies they are sorted chronologically.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical semantic gap: Evaluator only checks if dates ARE sorted, not if they WERE sorted by the agent
File is already sorted in source (per metadata), so evaluator returns 1.0 even if agent does nothing
Cannot distinguish between: (1) agent successfully sorted unsorted data vs (2) agent left already-sorted data unchanged
This is a property-based check that doesn't verify the actual task action was performed
Getter logic is correct: extracts column A dates, converts datetime to ISO format strings
Metric logic is correct: properly checks ascending order using sorted() comparison
Postconfig correctly saves file to persist changes
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Store original unsorted order in expected value to compare before/after state
Or ensure test data is actually unsorted initially (modify config to scramble dates first)
Or use a getter that extracts both original and current order, then metric verifies reordering occurred
Alternative: Add preconfig validation that file is NOT already sorted, fail test if it is
